questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Choose the correct article for the blank in the sentence:
"The complainant met with ___ honest police sub-inspector to record his statement."
questions.explanation: Word 'honest' ka pehla written letter consonant 'h' hai, lekin ye silent rehta hai. Word ka spoken opening sound /ˈɒnɪst/ ('o' vowel sound) hai. Rule ke mutabiq vocalic opening sound ke sath indefinite article 'AN' lagta hai. Isliye 'an honest police sub-inspector' correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Vowel sound demands 'AN' regardless of written consonant letter.
questions.hint: Check karein ki kya 'honest' bolte waqt 'h' pronounce hota hai ya 'o' vowel sound se shuru hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
"Dr. Sharma is a distinguished scholar teaching at ___ European university."
questions.explanation: Word 'European' written vowel 'E' se shuru hota hai, lekin iska spoken sound /jʊərəˈpiːən/ ('yu' consonant sound) hai. English phonetics mein initial consonantal sound /j/ ke aage article 'A' lagta hai, 'an' nahi. Isliye 'a European university' grammatically correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Consonant sound /j/ ('yu') demands 'A'.
questions.hint: 'European' bolte waqt opening sound 'yu' nikalta hai jo consonant sound hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate article:
"The victim wanted to lodge ___ FIR immediately after the robbery."
questions.explanation: Initialism 'FIR' ko bolte waqt pehla letter 'F' padha jata hai, jiska spoken sound /ef/ ('e' vowel sound se shuru) hota hai. Vocalic sound se shuru hone ke karan indefinite article 'AN' lagega: 'an FIR'. (Agar full form 'First Information Report' likha hota toh 'a' lagta).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Phonetic Sound Engine — Letter initials pronounced with initial vowel sound take 'AN'.
questions.hint: Letter 'F' ko pronounce karke dekhein: 'Ef' sound vowel se shuru hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Mountain Ranges vs Individual Mountain Peaks
questions.question:
Choose the option that correctly fills both blanks:
"___ Himalayas form the northern boundary of India, while ___ Mount Everest is the highest summit."
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges (chhoti-badi pahadiyon ki continuous chain) ke naam ke aage definite article 'The' lagta hai ('the Himalayas', 'the Alps'). Lekin kisi bhi individual mountain peak (single choti) ke naam ke aage article KABHI NAHI lagta ('Mount Everest', 'Mount Abu'). Isliye pehle blank mein 'The' aur doosre mein Zero Article (no article) aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Conventional Geography — Mountain Ranges take 'The'; Individual Peaks take Zero Article.
questions.hint: Mountain range vs single peak ke difference ko recall karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: General Uncountable Noun vs Particularized Context
questions.question:
Select the correct pair of articles:
"___ gold is a precious metal, but ___ gold mined in Kolar is known for its distinct purity."
questions.explanation: Pehle clause mein 'gold' general material noun hai jo poore sona category ko denote kar raha hai, isliye Zero Article (no article) lagega. Doosre clause mein 'gold' ke baad qualifying prepositional phrase 'mined in Kolar' laga hai, jisne use ek specific location ke sone tak restrict kar diya hai, isliye wahan definite article 'The' lagega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Zero Article Omission & Particularization Principle.
questions.hint: General meaning mein article omit hota hai; qualifying phrase judte hi 'The' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Institutional Purpose: Primary vs Secondary Visit
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct articles:
"The injured motorist was taken to ___ hospital for emergency surgery, and his brother went to ___ hospital to deliver his documents."
questions.explanation: Injured motorist hospital mein patient bankar medical treatment (primary functional purpose) ke liye gaya hai, isliye NO ARTICLE ('to hospital'). Motorist ka brother wahan documents deliver karne (incidental visitor / secondary purpose) gaya hai, isliye definite article 'the' aayega ('to the hospital').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Institutional Expressions — Primary function takes Zero Article; Secondary visit takes 'The'.
questions.hint: Pehle person patient hai (primary purpose), doosra person visitor hai (secondary purpose).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Few vs A Few in Negative vs Positive Context
questions.question:
Choose the appropriate quantifier:
"He is extremely unpopular among his colleagues because he has ___ manners and treats others disrespectfully."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka context clear negative tone establish kar raha hai ('extremely unpopular', 'treats others disrespectfully'). In manners ki scarcity/inadequacy (manners na ke barabar hona) express karne ke liye negative quantifier 'FEW' aayega. 'A few' positive availability denote karta hai jo context se contradict karega. 'Little' uncountable nouns ke sath lagta hai, jabki 'manners' plural countable hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Countable Quantifiers — 'Few' denotes negative scarcity ('almost none') with plural countable nouns.
questions.hint: Context negative hai (unpopular, disrespectful), isliye bina article wala negative quantifier aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Little vs A Little with Uncountable Nouns
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct determiner:
"Do not lose heart; with ___ patience and persistent effort, you will overcome these procedural hurdles."
questions.explanation: Noun 'patience' uncountable abstract noun hai. Sentence ka context encouraging aur positive hai ('Do not lose heart', 'you will overcome'). Positive modest amount (thoda sa dherya) express karne ke liye quantifier 'A LITTLE' use hota hai. 'Little' negative hopelessness batata jo sentence ke meaning ko ult-pult kar deta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Uncountable Quantifiers — 'A little' denotes positive existence ('some amount') with uncountable nouns.
questions.hint: Sentence encourage kar raha hai, isliye positive quantifier 'a little' aayega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: The Little in Exhaustive Scope Context
questions.question:
Identify the correct option for the blank:
"The destitute litigant spent ___ little money he had on travelling to the capital for the hearing."
questions.explanation: Noun 'money' ke sath 'little' laga hai aur uske baad defining clause 'he had' aayi hai. Litigant ke paas paise kam the, lekin wo saare ke saare jo uske paas the, usne travel par kharch kar diye (all of that small amount). Is exhaustive specific sense mein definite article 'The' lagta hai: 'the little money he had'.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: The Little Triad — 'The little' denotes 'all of that small quantity' followed by a defining clause.
questions.hint: Clause 'he had' specific bache huye saare amount ko refer kar rahi hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Polite Offers and Invitations with Some
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word to complete the question:
"Would you like ___ tea while you wait for the certified copies?"
questions.explanation: Ye sentence interrogative form mein hone ke bawajood ek POLITE OFFER (hospitality) hai, jahan speaker positive acceptance ('Yes') expect karta hai. Pragmatic grammar rule ke hisaab se polite offers aur requests mein hamesha 'SOME' use hota hai, 'any' nahi. 'Any' cold aur purely investigative inquiries mein lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Some vs Any — Polite offers and requests starting with 'Would you like...?' take 'SOME'.
questions.hint: 'Would you like...?' ek mehmaannawazi (offer) hai, na ki investigative interrogation.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.subtopic: Much vs Many Concord on Uncountable Noun
questions.question: Select the sentence with NO grammatical error in determiner usage:

options.text: The clerk gave me many useful informations about the court fees.
The clerk gave me much useful information about the court fees.
The clerk gave me an useful information about the court fees.
The clerk gave me many useful advices about the court fees.

questions.explanation: 'Information' uncountable mass noun hai. Iska plural (*informations) nahi banta aur iske aage 'many' ya 'an' nahi lagta. Uncountable nouns ke sath quantity express karne ke liye 'much' lagta hai: 'much useful information'. Option (A) mein 'many' aur 'informations' dono galat hain; Option (C) mein 'an' galat hai; Option (D) mein 'many advices' galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10 & RC-02: Quantity Concord & Uncountable Noun Rules.
questions.hint: 'Information' uncountable noun hai jiska plural nahi banta aur jiske sath 'much' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10

questions.topic: Use of Articles, Determiners and Prepositions
questions.question: Spot the grammatically correct sentence involving distributive determiners:

options.text: Each of the candidates were interviewed by the selection committee.
Each of the candidates was interviewed by the selection committee.
Every candidates was interviewed by the selection committee.
Neither of the five officers was held accountable for the lapse.

questions.explanation: 'Each of the' ke baad noun hamesha plural ('candidates') hota hai, LEKIN VERB HAMESHA SINGULAR ('was interviewed') hoti hai, kyunki sentence ka actual head subject 'Each' (singular) hai. Option (A) mein plural verb 'were' lagayi gayi hai jo galat hai. Option (C) mein 'Every' ke turant baad plural noun 'candidates' lagaya gaya hai (*Every student hota hai). Option (D) mein paanch (5) officers ke liye 'Neither' lagaya gaya hai, jabki 3 ya zyada ke liye 'None' use hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Distributive Determiners — 'Each of the + Plural Noun + Singular Verb'.
questions.hint: 'Each of the' ke baad verb singular aati hai, aur 'Neither' sirf 2 ke liye use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L10
